caption: The north west tip belonged to the McNamees. Connel McNamee held it in 1825, and John McNamee in 1831 and again in the 1850s. The McNamees had one household in 1901 and one in 1911, and none in 1926.
In 1825 James, Owen, Hugh and Daniel Cassidy held 21 plots between them. James, Daniel and Hugh were still there in 1831, with Peter, and Cassidys held land in the 1850s.
The McGintys were the largest family on the land. In 1825 Neil, Hugh, Owen, James and Edward McGinty held plots, and Hugh, Edward and Owen were still there in 1831 and in the 1850s.
Patrick, Edward and Felim Gildea were on the land in 1825, in 1831 and in the 1850s. The clerks wrote the name Kildea in the first two. Jeremiah Gildea appears in the 1850s.
The McAnaw homestead is the fixed point. Michael and James were there in 1825, 1831 and the 1850s, and the name was written McAna, then McArea, then McKenna.
The Mullens shared ground with the Gildeas and with the Monaghans in 1825, and again in the 1850s. The Monaghans were written Meaghan in 1825. Hugh Monaghan was named in 1831 and in the 1850s.
A widow named Thomas held ground in 1825, Patrick Thomas in 1831 and Catherine Thomas in the 1850s. There were four Thomas households in 1901 and three in 1911.
Three names are new in the 1850s: Connell Harvey, Hugh Gethins and Hugh Corrigan. None of them is named in 1825 or 1831. The Harveys were still in the townland in 1901 and 1911.
